title: What Happened, and Who Did It

lessons.title: वह गया (vah gayā) — the past, by who did it
lessons.gloss: he went — the past of a verb with no object, agreeing with the one who went

segments.text: Before the new one: say turning over and a stretch. (karvaṭ, aṅgṛāī.) Then the host's question खाना खाया?, "have you eaten?" Its खाया is a past, and this chapter builds every past like it.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the past, by who did it

segments.text: कल मैं बाज़ार गया। kal maiṁ bāzār gayā. — "Yesterday I went to the market."
With a past, कल is yesterday. गया is जाना in the past, with no है after it. Its ending follows the one who went, as अच्छा, अच्छी, अच्छे follow a noun:

utterances: who went: a man: मैं, वह. the past: गया (gayā).
who went: a woman. the past: गई (gaī).
who went: men, or आप, तुम, हम. the past: गए (gae).
who went: women. the past: गईं (gaīṁ).

blocks.title: You'll want to know: how a stem takes the ending

segments.text: Most verbs put the ending on the stem: बैठना becomes वह बैठा, वह बैठी (vah baiṭhā, vah baiṭhī). A stem ending in a vowel adds -या for a man: आना becomes आया, आई (āyā, āī). Two change the stem: जाना becomes गया, and होना becomes हुआ, हुई (huā, huī): क्या हुआ?, "what happened?"
"Did not": मैं नहीं गया (maiṁ nahīṃ gayā). A bare stem with गया says the change is complete, as in देर हो गई and वह सो गया (vah so gayā), "he fell asleep".

lessons.title: उसने रोटी खाई (usne roṭī khāī) — the past that follows the thing
lessons.gloss: he ate a roti — with an object, the doer takes ने and the verb agrees with the thing

segments.text: Say "she went". (vah gaī.) खाना खाया? leaves the eater out; this lesson puts the eater in.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the doer takes ने

segments.text: उसने खाना खाया। usne khānā khāyā. — "He (or she) ate the meal."

With a verb that has an object, such as eating, reading or saying, the past changes: the doer takes ने (ne). The pronouns fuse with it: मैंने, तुमने, आपने, उसने, हमने, उन्होंने (maiṁne, tumne, āpne, usne, hamne, unhoṁne), the last from वे. A name takes ने after it: मीरा ने. उसने is "he" or "she"; the verb no longer says which.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the verb follows the thing

segments.text: मीरा ने रोटी खाई। Mīrā ne roṭī khāī. — "Mira ate a roti."

रोटी is feminine, so खाई, whoever ate it. With खाना, masculine, खाया; with books, मैंने किताबें पढ़ीं (maiṁne kitābeṁ paṛhīṁ). When the thing takes को, or there is none, the verb stays -आ: उसने मीरा को देखा (usne Mīrā ko dekhā), "he saw Mira".

utterances: sentence: वह गई — no thing. the verb follows: the one who went.
sentence: उसने रोटी खाई (usne roṭī khāī) — ने and a thing. the verb follows: the thing.
sentence: उसने मीरा को देखा — the thing has को. the verb follows: nothing: -आ.

segments.text: Four verbs make this past their own way, for a masculine thing and a feminine one: किया / की, दिया / दी, लिया / ली, पिया / पी (kiyā / kī, diyā / dī, liyā / lī, piyā / pī), from करना, देना, लेना and पीना.

कहना (kahnā), "to say", is regular. Your क्या कहा? was its past: उसने कहा कि वह कल आएगा (usne kahā ki vah kal āegā), "he said he would come tomorrow". लाना, "to bring", never takes ने: वह फल लाया (vah phal lāyā).

feedback.correct: ne on the doer, and the verb follows roṭī and kitāb, both feminine.
feedback.incorrect: With an object, the doer takes ne and the verb follows the thing: roṭī khāī, kitāb paṛhī.

segments.text: Why खाई in उसने रोटी खाई (usne roṭī khāī)? (रोटी is feminine.) Now the other way: "he ate the meal"? (उसने खाना खाया.) Why देखा in उसने मीरा को देखा? (The thing has को.) "He said"? (उसने कहा.)

segments.text: Which past follows the one who went? (A verb with no thing: वह गई.) Which follows the thing? (The past with ने: मीरा ने रोटी खाई.) Now the other way round: in उसने खाना खाया, which word tells you that खाना is masculine? (खाया.) And when the thing takes को? (The verb stays -आ: उसने मीरा को देखा.)
